title: Dunking on Dating App Profiles Is Content Gold. People Are Getting Sick of It
gist: Hinge is testing screenshot protection in India, reigniting debate over the practice of screenshotting and mocking dating profiles for social media content. The piece weighs privacy and shame against women's safety uses, and the company says there are no plans to expand to the US.

insights.claim: Hinge is piloting screenshot blocking in India on surfaces with personally identifiable profile info (Discover, Likes You, Standouts), the first such Hinge feature, while Raya and Grindr already offer it.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Dating apps are adding privacy features to counter content-driven harassment; watch whether Hinge expands.
insights.quote: the India pilot is the first iteration of it for Hinge

insights.claim: Hinge says the India test is meant to build trust among singles and with the platform; results will determine whether it expands, but there are no current plans for the US or other regions.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.quote: there are no current plans to greenlight screenshot protection in US or other regions

insights.claim: Hinge, with 30 million users, frames screenshot protection alongside Comment Filter and Did This Bother You? as ways to help daters control how personal details are shared, while still allowing screenshots of messages for safety reports.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Safety-reporting carve-out shows the trade-off with privacy.

insights.claim: Creators on TikTok and X accounts like @hingestrange have built brands screenshotting bizarre profile prompts, cringe lines and red flags.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Dating-app content is a durable creator niche that platforms now face pressure over.

insights.claim: Dating coach Chad Franklin posts clients' private messages to his 512,000 TikTok followers, though he says he tries to block names and faces; he argues apps have no duty to protect users: 'If you enter the dragon’s den, you may get bit by the dragon.'
